subject: Clarify default data horizon and what we persist vs transient
messages:
From: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@brightbank.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: security@brightbank.com
Date: 2027-10-12T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Clarify what Redwood retains by default for API calls

Hi Rafael,

We’re kicking off procurement and the security team has a few questions about default retention and residency for Redwood-hosted API calls. Specifically: 

- What is retained by default for a standard hosted API request (request metadata, full prompt text, model outputs, intermediate tokens/streaming fragments)?
- Do prompts count as "customer-provided data" and are they persisted by default?
- Are derivative artifacts (e.g., embeddings, reranks, KV cache snapshots) stored and for how long?
- What is the default retention horizon and can BrightBank opt for shorter or immediate deletion via API?
- Residency: can we ensure requests from EU regions are stored only in EU?

We’ll need clear, procurement-friendly language and any artifacts (SOC2 / retention diagrams) you can share.

Thanks,
Oliver
Oliver Grant
Director, Cloud Security (BrightBank)

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@brightbank.com>
Cc: security@brightbank.com
Date: 2027-10-12T10:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify what Redwood retains by default for API calls

Hi Oliver — thanks for the clear list. Quick summary up top, details below and I’ve attached a short summary PDF and a sample delete API request.

Short answer (tl;dr)
- Default hosted retention window: 60 days for request/response artifacts unless the customer opts into a different policy.
- Prompts: raw prompt text is retained by default for debugging/quality and to support reproducibility; customers can opt-out at account or route level.
- Outputs: model outputs are treated like request artifacts and are retained for the same default window.
- Derivatives: embeddings and reranking artifacts are stored only if the customer explicitly requests embedding generation or chooses to persist them; default is ephemeral unless the embedding API call uses the "persist": true flag.
- KV caches and transient runtime artifacts are not persisted to long-term storage by default; they live in memory or ephemeral storage tied to the serving instance.

Details
- Retention: The hosted default retention horizon is 60 calendar days from ingestion. After that window artifacts are purged from our customer-facing telemetry store and queued for TTL-based tombstone deletion across backups. We maintain short-term logs for operational debugging (rotating cycles) but those are inaccessible via the console beginning at the 60-day mark.
- Prompts vs outputs: Both are considered request/response artifacts when submitted via the API. "Prompt" (the input text) and "output" (model-generated text) are indexed the same for retention/ audit purposes. Customers can opt out of storing prompts by setting the account-level "store_prompts": false flag or per-request header X-Redwood-Store: none.
- Embeddings/Derivatives: Calls to the embeddings endpoints produce artifacts that, by default, are ephemeral unless you include the persist flag or call the embeddings-store API. If persisted, those objects are retained according to the account retention policy (default 60 days).
- Deletion API / immediate purge: We provide a synchronous deletion endpoint (/v1/retention/delete) for single-request deletion requests and an asynchronous purge job for bulk deletes. Sample curl attached (Retention-API-sample-request.txt). Note that deletion from user-visible stores is immediate, but full propagation to backups and audit indexes can take up to 48 hours.
- Residency controls: For hosted customers we provide region routing and data residency controls. Requests originating from EU regions are stored in EU data stores by default when the account is configured with EU residency. Dedicated and Private deployments provide stricter residency guarantees.

Attachments included:
- RB-DataRetention-Summary.pdf (short FAQ + diagram)
- Retention-API-sample-request.txt (curl examples)

If you want formal legal wording for procurement or a SOC2 artifact, I’ll loop in our security/compliance lead. Happy to set a quick sync.

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Hi Oliver — looping in Kimberley (security & compliance) and happy to provide the formal language for procurement. Below is a concise paragraph you can drop into an exhibit, followed by implementation specifics and links to the artifacts we’ve provided. Attachments include a one-page SOC2 summary and a short sample retention API request.

Procurement-friendly paragraph (suggested exhibit language)
"Redwood Inference retains customer-request and generated response artifacts in its hosted telemetry store for a configurable retention period. The default retention horizon for hosted accounts is 60 days from ingestion. Customers may opt out of storing input prompts at the account level or per-request by using the account flag or request header: setting store_prompts = false prevents the long-term persistence of prompt text in Redwood’s telemetry and analytics pipelines. For persisted derivative objects (for example, explicitly-stored embeddings), the same account-level retention policy applies. Redwood exposes synchronous and asynchronous deletion APIs; deletion requests are processed immediately in user-facing stores with audit logs generated for each deletion operation. Complete removal from backups and historical replicas can take up to 48 hours, and Redwood will provide deletion confirmation receipts for records deleted via the API upon request."

Implementation specifics / clarifications
- Prompts opt-out: setting the account flag (store_prompts = false) or adding header X-Redwood-Store: none on a per-request basis prevents prompt text from being ingested into long-term analytics and telemetry pipelines. This also suppresses prompt text from being indexed for internal quality tooling.
- Deletion audit: each deletion request (sync or purge job) produces an immutable audit entry (request id + timestamp) visible to the customer via the Console > Security > Retention > Deletion Activity. We can provide signed deletion receipts for procurement on a case-by-case basis; please flag which records require receipts.
- Propagation window: 48 hours is the upper bound for full propagation to all backups/replicas; user-visible store deletion happens immediately.
- Residency: per-account residency controls route and store data in the selected region (EU/US/APAC). Dedicated and Private customers can enforce on-prem or VPC-only residency.

Artifacts attached/links

- RB-DataRetention-Summary.pdf (diagram + FAQ)
- Retention-API-sample-request.txt (curl examples and sample payloads)

- Happy to set a short call with Kimberly to walk through technical controls and the deletion/audit flow.
